title: Capture tape visitation and space
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes and Boolean output, and let $H$ be a machine with $k+1$ work tapes and a Boolean output. Suppose a map from the states of $M$ to those of $H$ and a return state are chosen, and at every mapped state the transition of $H$ agrees with the capture transform of the transition of $M$. For any Boolean input, initial configuration $c_0$, Boolean words $p,o$, and time $t$, suppose $M$ is not halted at any time strictly less than $t$. Then each of the first $k$ work tapes of $H$, started from the capture image of $c_0$, visits exactly the same head positions through time $t$ as the corresponding tape of $M$, and uses the same amount of space; the additional tape of $H$ uses at most the output length of $M$ at time $t$ minus its initial output length, plus one.
hypotheses_covered: Two machines with $k$ and $k+1$ work tapes, respectively
State map and designated return state
Transition agreement with the capture transform for every state, input symbol, and work-tape reading
The original machine is not halted at any time $t'<t$
